note: Generic component with one install script and one bound artifact maps to one native manifest; ComponentPublisher is reported, not silently dropped.

First-match manifest order is preserved; Windows is omitted and reported; AWS amd64 maps to native x86_64; a manifest without Platform matches all platforms; npm-style comparator ranges inside the native grammar translate to recipe 1.1.
An AWS-populated SHA-256 digest must equal the operator's authenticated binding; default permissions are accepted.
A digest that differs from the binding is rejected.
Only SHA-256 digests can be cross-checked.

run/shutdown map to the merged SF-014 supervisor; {artifacts:path}/<Uri basename> becomes {artifact} and {work:path} becomes {work}. Restart/timeout behaviour differs from AWS and is reported, not hidden.

DefaultConfiguration becomes native recipe 1.2 defaults, delivered as the {configuration} file and $SUIFLEET_CONFIGURATION; existing device values are kept and new defaults fill gaps, as in Greengrass. Dependencies stay in the same 1.2 recipe.
Shell parameter braces are not recipe variables and pass through unchanged.

Lifecycle.run: while true; do echo "${HOME}"; sleep 5; done

lifecycle.run: while true; do echo "${HOME}"; sleep 5; done

note: The native workspace holds only the bound artifact, so other artifact-directory paths cannot keep their meaning.
Only the exact Uri basename maps to {artifact}.
There is no unarchive support.
Native substitutions are shell-quoted; a variable inside quotes would change meaning.
AWS leaves {work} literal but the native daemon would substitute it.
Native install commands do not substitute {work}.
Rejections list every reason; BootstrapOnRollback has no native equivalent and is rejected even after SF-014.
Background startup services have no native equivalent; shutdown needs a supervised run.
Per-step timeouts are not expressible in the native recipe; device-wide limits apply.
Native commands get a cleared environment; Setenv has no equivalent.
Native commands receive the whole configuration as a file ({configuration}), never an inline value; {configuration:/pointer} has no equivalent and is rejected with guidance.
Greengrass configuration keys are case-insensitive; native keys are case-sensitive, so keys differing only in case would split one AWS value in two.
Native configuration depth is at most 32 (the defaults object is level 1); deeper defaults are rejected before publication rather than failing on every device.
Native configuration reaches only install or run commands; a manifest without either cannot receive it.
{configuration} is literal text to Greengrass but a native substitution.

accessControl authorizes the AWS IPC protocol, which is not implemented; native IPC ACLs are operator configuration, never recipe privileges. The pub/sub policy is reported as the equivalent operator ACL (exact topics only).
Glob topics, MQTT proxy and other IPC services have no native ACL equivalent and are listed as unmapped; exact pub/sub topics map to publish/subscribe.
Cross-component variables have no native equivalent.
There is no AWS IoT thing; the translator must not substitute a different identity silently.
No Greengrass kernel root exists.
Root escalation is outside the SF-009 runtime boundary.
Skipif is not translated.
Greengrass bootstrap with restart exit codes (100/101) has no native equivalent; SF-014 lists it as not yet supported.
Lambda components belong to the SF-038 adapter decision.
Nucleus plugins cannot run.
SF-038 classification: TokenExchangeService maps to the unimplemented credential-provider adapter (SF-057), so the recipe is rejected and the classification reported.
SF-038 'replace': the daemon replaces the nucleus, so the dependency is dropped and reported, never silently; other dependencies keep native rules.
Roadmap gaps and natively packaged AWS components are rejected with their SF-038 classification.
npm x-ranges, hyphen ranges and || are outside the native comparator grammar.
Disjunctions are rejected rather than narrowed.
Java regular-expression platform matching is not reproduced.
architecture.detail, runtime and custom platform attributes are rejected.
Runtime selection is AWS-specific.
Unknown OS values are rejected, not treated as wildcards.
Recipes for omitted platforms only are rejected.
The native catalog rejects duplicate OS/architecture pairs.
Native artifacts are single opaque files.
Artifact permissions are not translated.
Every artifact needs an operator-supplied Walrus blob and authenticated SHA-256 binding.
Native recipes bind exactly one artifact.
Native recipes require an artifact.
Global lifecycle selections are not translated.
Only RecipeFormatVersion 2020-01-25 exists.
Unknown top-level keys are rejected.
ComponentVersion must be SemVer.
Native component-name grammar applies.
Unknown interpolation namespaces are rejected.
The nucleus-provided environment (SVCUID, AWS_GG_*, AWS_IOT_THING_NAME, AWS_REGION, ...) is absent: the daemon clears the environment.
Correction to the SF-028 subset: a native recipe without install or run hands its artifact to the platform updater; an AWS artifact-only manifest never does, so it is rejected.
ComponentDescription must be a string in the native recipe.
Component removal retires management but does not uninstall.
Native restart policy replaces recover; it is not translated silently.
A YAML recipe in the AWS developer-guide shape parses to the pinned JSON value and translates; a missing architecture means any.

# The AWS developer guide's YAML recipe shape
RecipeFormatVersion: '2020-01-25'
ComponentName: com.example.Hello
ComponentVersion: '1.0.0'
ComponentDescription: My first AWS IoT Greengrass component.
ComponentPublisher: Amazon
ComponentConfiguration:
  DefaultConfiguration:
    Message: world
    Count: 3
    Enabled: true
Manifests:
  - Platform:
      os: linux
    Lifecycle:
      run: |
        python3 -u {artifacts:path}/hello.tar
    Artifacts:
